title: Bengaluru Triple Murder Accused Used AI Chatbot for Six Months to Plan Killings
excerpt: Police say Kenneth, 25, consulted an AI chatbot about killing methods, body disposal, and evidence removal before the June stabbing of his partner's parents and sister. Investigators have now written to the AI company seeking his full chat history.
body:
• Bengaluru police have approached an AI company for chat records after discovering accused Kenneth allegedly used a chatbot for six months to plan the June 22 triple murder in KR Puram.
  • Kenneth and his live-in partner Shwetha, 24, are accused of stabbing her father Somasundar (52), mother Muthulakshmi (48), and sister Supriya (19) to death in their Seegehalli apartment.
  • The accused allegedly queried the chatbot about killing methods, bloodstain removal, body disposal, and whether a cloud kitchen furnace could incinerate remains.
  • The case adds to a growing global pattern of AI chatbots being implicated in violent crime planning, raising fresh questions about platform safety guardrails.

Bengaluru police investigating the sensational triple murder at a Seegehalli apartment have written to an artificial intelligence company seeking the accused's full chat history, after discovering he allegedly relied on an AI chatbot for nearly six months to plan the killings, according to officials.

Kenneth, 25, who has been arrested along with his live-in partner Shwetha, 24, allegedly used the chatbot at every stage of the crime — from researching methods to kill and dispose of bodies, to finding ways to erase evidence, police said on Tuesday.

The Murders

The killings came to light on June 22 when Somasundar, 52, his wife Muthulakshmi, 48, and their younger daughter Supriya, 19, were found stabbed to death inside a flat in Seegehalli under the KR Puram police station limits. All three were members of Shwetha's family.

https://x.com/dhanyarajendran/status/2079053673808986380

According to the Hindustan Times, investigators believe the original plan targeted only Muthulakshmi, but the plot escalated when Somasundar and Supriya arrived at the apartment unexpectedly. Kenneth allegedly lured Muthulakshmi to the flat and stabbed her repeatedly. When her husband and younger daughter arrived, they too were attacked.

Despite suffering grievous injuries, Somasundar managed to drag himself to the staircase, where neighbours spotted him and called police. In his dying declaration at the hospital, he identified Shwetha and Kenneth as the attackers and pleaded with officers to save his wife and daughter before succumbing to his injuries, according to the Times of India.

AI-Assisted Planning

A senior police officer told reporters that Kenneth had consulted the AI chatbot throughout a six-month period preceding the murders. His queries allegedly covered killing methods, techniques for disposing of bodies, how to remove bloodstains, and whether a furnace built for a proposed cloud kitchen business could be used to incinerate the remains.

During interrogation, Kenneth allegedly admitted that a minor disagreement had prompted him to target Shwetha's family and confessed to depending heavily on the chatbot for guidance. Police have now formally requested digital evidence of his conversations from the AI company to corroborate his statements.

"Our investigation indicates that the original plan was to target only Muthulakshmi. After the murder, the accused intended to move the body to another rented location to avoid suspicion."

— Bengaluru Police, per Hindustan Times

Financial Disputes and Isolation

Investigators have traced the killings to financial disputes and strained family relations. According to the Times of India, Shwetha had borrowed approximately ₹50 lakh from her mother to fund Kenneth's cloud kitchen venture. When the money ran out without a viable business to show for it, fears over repayment mounted.

Earlier reports from the Dainik Bhaskar placed the disputed amount at ₹30 lakh, describing it as a loan taken from a private bank that triggered family conflict. Shwetha, a software engineer, had been living with Kenneth in a separate apartment in the Sai Green complex for about two months before the murders.

Psychological assessments conducted during the investigation revealed that Kenneth suffered from severe social isolation. Police said Shwetha had financially supported him throughout and had gradually distanced herself from friends and family, eventually losing her job in the IT sector.

Arrest and Aftermath

After the murders, the couple allegedly stole cash and silver ornaments from the apartment before fleeing to Puducherry, about 220 kilometres away. Bengaluru police formed 10 special teams and tracked them down within days. Shwetha was arrested from a Puducherry hotel on June 24, and Kenneth was secured the following day. Both were remanded to police custody.

During questioning, Shwetha reportedly told investigators she had "lived like an orphan" and harboured deep resentment toward her mother, according to NewsX.

Part of a Disturbing Global Pattern

The Bengaluru case joins a growing list of criminal investigations worldwide where AI chatbot records have become critical evidence. In April 2026, a University of South Florida student was charged with double murder after prosecutors revealed he had asked ChatGPT about disposing of a body days before two doctoral students were killed. In South Korea, a 21-year-old woman was charged in connection with serial poisonings after police found she had queried ChatGPT about whether mixing drugs could kill someone.

These cases have intensified pressure on AI companies to strengthen safety guardrails and establish clearer protocols for flagging potentially dangerous queries to law enforcement — a debate that remains unresolved across jurisdictions.

What's Next

The investigation now hinges on the AI company's response to the police request for Kenneth's chatbot conversations. That digital evidence could prove crucial in establishing premeditation and the full extent of planning behind the killings. Both accused remain in police custody, and charges are expected to be filed under multiple sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
